Dr. PRJ Gangadharam Endowment Award Presented to Dr. Urvashi B Singh
Tuesday, 31 March 2026
834 Hits
The Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS), Sevagram, organised the distinguished Dr. PRJ Gangadharam Award Ceremony on 27th March 2026 to acknowledge exceptional contributions in the field of tuberculosis research and control. On this occasion, Dr. Urvashi B. Singh, Professor of Microbiology at AIIMS and former DDG (TB), Central TB Division, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, as well as Director, NTI Bengaluru, was honoured with this prestigious award. The award was presented by Shri P. L. Tapadia (President, Kasturba Health Society) in recognition of her exemplary contributions to tuberculosis prevention, treatment, and policy advocacy.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Singh emphasised the importance of grassroots impact, stating,
“Unless we reach the common man, what we do doesn’t really matter.”
Dr. Singh’s work has played a pivotal role in strengthening efforts towards tuberculosis elimination, both at the national and global levels. Her leadership across public health initiatives, clinical research, and policy implementation has had a significant and enduring impact on TB control programmes in India.
The ceremony was attended by Dr. B. S. Garg (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society), Dr AK Shukla (Dean, MGIMS), Dr. Poonam Shivkumar Varma (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital), Dr. P. Narang (Advisor in Microbiology & TB Research and Organising Chairperson of the Award) and Dr. Vijayshree Khairkar (Organising Secretary and Head, Department of Microbiology). The event also witnessed the presence of senior faculty members, heads of departments, consultants, staff, residents, and nursing personnel.
Instituted in memory of Dr. PRJ Gangadharam, a renowned figure in tuberculosis research, the endowment award recognises Indian scientists who have made significant contributions to TB control and aims to encourage young researchers to engage in this critical field. Dr. Singh was felicitated with a citation, a certificate of honour, and a cash prize of ₹25,000 in recognition of her outstanding work.
